name: LBNL 2014 US PUE by space type - hyperscale: 1.2 (component sum: 1 | 0.02 | - | 0.16 | 0.02 -> IT 1, transformer 0.02, no UPS term, cooling 0.16, lighting 0.02)
unit: dimensionless PUE ratio (total facility energy / IT equipment energy), 2014 baseline. Not an accuracy score and not a speedup: 1.0 means the facility overhead is nil.
methodology: MODELED BASELINE, TABLE 4 ('2014 PUE by Space Type') of the DOE/BL United States Data Center Energy Usage Report. The row decomposes total PUE into IT (=1 by definition), transformer, UPS, cooling and lighting contributions, and the components sum to the stated total - which is how the table was verified here rather than trusted. Space types are IDC-defined and span both internal enterprise spaces and service-provider spaces; the report states service provider data centers are INCLUSIVE of colocation facilities. This is the most granular public per-facility-type PUE breakdown available from an authoritative US government source. engine_id is ollama only as a schema placeholder: facility metric, no engine.
notes:
Hyperscale: 1.2, the best space type, and structurally different rather than marginally better - no UPS loss term at all (distribution runs without double conversion) and cooling down to 0.16. THIS IS WHY THE NATIONAL AVERAGE IMPROVED: hyperscale is both the most efficient space type AND where nearly all server growth since 2010 went, so the national average moved as a composition effect. Any extrapolation of hyperscale PUE to a general deployment should assume you are not building hyperscale. CAVEAT ON AGE: these are 2014 values and the 2016 report frames the 2020 trajectory separately (dynamic range, consolidation). For a current planning number prefer the 2025 Update's 1.45 national all-equipment average. The 2014 table is retained because the modern public sources publish only fleet or national AVERAGES - this table is the only public breakdown that shows a colocation-class facility is closer to 1.9 than to 1.2.

METRIC CORRECTION 2026-10-05 (schema authority pass, agent w5-schema). Value UNCHANGED; `metric` moved quality -> dimensionless_ratio. PUE is a ratio by DEFINITION (total facility energy / IT equipment energy) and carries no faster/slower reading, so it is a dimensionless_ratio rather than a speedup_ratio. It was previously filed as `quality`, the catch-all that gotcha bench-metric-enum-hides-a-dimensionless-ratio names as the reason `quality` cannot be trusted as a semantic filter: that key was spanning accuracy deltas in percentage points, PUE ratios and power ratios simultaneously.
